+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import duckdb
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+import pandas as pd
+
+
+OUT = Path("out")

+    "font.family": "DejaVu Sans",

+    "xtick.labelsize": 9,

+    SELECT
+      year(crash_date)::INTEGER AS year,
+      count(*)::INTEGER AS brooklyn_reported_crashes,
+      sum(coalesce(number_of_pedestrians_injured, 0))::INTEGER AS pedestrians_injured,
+      sum(coalesce(number_of_pedestrians_killed, 0))::INTEGER AS pedestrians_killed,
+      count(*) FILTER (WHERE coalesce(number_of_pedestrians_injured, 0) > 0

+          AS crashes_with_pedestrian_casualty
+    FROM read_parquet('data/crashes.parquet')
+    WHERE borough = 'BROOKLYN'
+      AND crash_date >= DATE '2013-01-01'
+      AND crash_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
+    GROUP BY year
+    ORDER BY year
+""").fetchdf()

+orange = "#D55E00"
+gray = "#5F6B73"
+grid = "#DCE3E8"
+
+

+    ax.set_xticks(years)
+    ax.set_xticklabels(years, rotation=45, ha="right")
+    ax.grid(axis="y", color=grid, linewidth=0.8)
+    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
+    ax.tick_params(axis="both", length=0, pad=7)
+
+
+def footer(fig, text):
+    fig.text(0.10, 0.035, text, fontsize=8.5, color=gray)
+    fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.10, right=0.96, top=0.82, bottom=0.20)
+
+

+        marker="o", markersize=6)
+ax.fill_between(years, annual["pedestrian_casualties"], color=blue, alpha=0.10)
+ax.set_title("Pedestrian casualties in Brooklyn are below 2013,\nbut have risen since 2020", loc="left", color=navy, pad=18)
+ax.text(0, 1.015, "Pedestrians injured or killed in police-reported crashes, by year",
+        transform=ax.transAxes, color=gray, fontsize=10)
+ax.set_ylabel("People injured or killed")
+base_axis(ax)
+first, last = annual.iloc[0], annual.iloc[-1]
+ax.annotate(f"{int(first.pedestrian_casualties):,}", (first.year, first.pedestrian_casualties),
+            xytext=(0, 12), textcoords="offset points", ha="center", color=navy, fontsize=10, weight="bold")
+ax.annotate(f"{int(last.pedestrian_casualties):,}", (last.year, last.pedestrian_casualties),
+            xytext=(0, 12), textcoords="offset points", ha="center", color=navy, fontsize=10, weight="bold")

+plt.close(fig)
+
+values1 = annual[["year", "pedestrians_injured", "pedestrians_killed", "pedestrian_casualties"]]
+values1.to_csv(OUT / "values_1.csv", index=False)

+bars = ax.bar(years, annual["pedestrians_killed"], color=orange, width=0.72)

+ax.text(0, 1.015, "Pedestrians killed in police-reported crashes, by year",
+        transform=ax.transAxes, color=gray, fontsize=10)
+ax.set_ylabel("Pedestrian deaths")
+ax.set_ylim(0, max(annual["pedestrians_killed"]) * 1.23)
+base_axis(ax)
+for i in [0, len(bars) - 1]:
+    bar = bars[i]
+    ax.annotate(f"{int(bar.get_height())}", (bar.get_x() + bar.get_width() / 2, bar.get_height()),
+                xytext=(0, 6), textcoords="offset points", ha="center", color=navy, fontsize=10, weight="bold")
+footer(fig, "Source: NYC police-reported motor vehicle crashes. Brooklyn; full calendar years 2013–2025. The dataset does not identify pedestrian exposure.")
+fig.savefig(OUT / "option_2.png", dpi=180, facecolor="white")
+plt.close(fig)
+
+values2 = annual[["year", "pedestrians_killed"]]
+values2.to_csv(OUT / "values_2.csv", index=False)
+

+ax.plot(years, annual["share_crashes_with_pedestrian_casualty_pct"], color=navy,

+ax.set_title("A larger share of Brooklyn crash reports involved\na pedestrian casualty in 2025 than in 2013", loc="left", color=navy, pad=18)
+ax.text(0, 1.015, "Crash reports with ≥1 pedestrian injured or killed, as a share of all Brooklyn crash reports",
+        transform=ax.transAxes, color=gray, fontsize=10)
+ax.set_ylabel("Share of crash reports (%)")
+base_axis(ax)
+ax.set_ylim(0, max(annual["share_crashes_with_pedestrian_casualty_pct"]) * 1.25)
+for row in [annual.iloc[0], annual.iloc[-1]]:
+    pct = row.share_crashes_with_pedestrian_casualty_pct
+    ax.annotate(f"{pct:.1f}%", (row.year, pct), xytext=(0, 12), textcoords="offset points",
+                ha="center", color=navy, fontsize=10, weight="bold")
+footer(fig, "Source: NYC police-reported motor vehicle crashes. Brooklyn; full calendar years 2013–2025. This is a share of reported crashes, not a pedestrian risk rate.")
+fig.savefig(OUT / "option_3.png", dpi=180, facecolor="white")
+plt.close(fig)
+
+values3 = annual[["year", "brooklyn_reported_crashes", "crashes_with_pedestrian_casualty",
+                  "share_crashes_with_pedestrian_casualty_pct"]]
+values3.to_csv(OUT / "values_3.csv", index=False, float_format="%.6f")
+
+options = {
+    "options": [
+        {
+            "id": 1,
+            "metric": "Annual pedestrian casualties (injured + killed)",
+            "denominator": "None; annual count of people reported injured or killed",
+            "grouping": "Calendar year, Brooklyn",
+            "chart_type": "Line chart",
+            "reason": "A count of people harmed gives a direct, broad measure of the annual human toll.",
+            "probability": 0.45,
+            "answer": "Brooklyn reported 2,874 pedestrian casualties in 2025 (2,835 injured and 39 killed), 21.7% fewer than the 3,671 reported in 2013, though the count rose from 1,798 in 2020.",
+            "interpretation": "This framing answers whether the annual number of pedestrians injured or killed changed: it was lower in 2025 than in 2013, after rising for five consecutive years from 2020. It is a defensible measure of the reported human toll, but without pedestrian counts or travel exposure it cannot establish whether an individual pedestrian's risk improved."
+        },
+        {
+            "id": 2,
+            "metric": "Annual pedestrian deaths",
+            "denominator": "None; annual count of pedestrians killed",
+            "grouping": "Calendar year, Brooklyn",
+            "chart_type": "Bar chart",
+            "reason": "Deaths are the most severe outcome and merit a separate trend from the much larger injury count.",
+            "probability": 0.35,
+            "answer": "Brooklyn reported 39 pedestrian deaths in 2025, 30.0% more than the 30 reported in 2013; the annual count ranged from 17 to 46 over 2013–2025.",
+            "interpretation": "This framing answers the most severe part of road safety: reported pedestrian deaths were higher in 2025 than in 2013, despite substantial year-to-year variation. A fatality count is a clear measure of deaths, but it does not capture nonfatal injuries or adjust for how many people walked."
+        },
+        {
+            "id": 3,
+            "metric": "Share of reported Brooklyn crashes with at least one pedestrian injured or killed",
+            "denominator": "All police-reported Brooklyn motor vehicle crashes in that year",
+            "grouping": "Calendar year, Brooklyn",
+            "chart_type": "Line chart",
+            "reason": "The share puts pedestrian-casualty crashes in context of the number of all reported crashes, rather than comparing counts alone.",
+            "probability": 0.20,
+            "answer": "Pedestrian-casualty crashes made up 11.4% of Brooklyn's reported crashes in 2025, up from 7.4% in 2013 (an increase of 3.9 percentage points).",
+            "interpretation": "This framing answers whether pedestrian-casualty crashes became more common within the pool of reported Brooklyn crashes: their share was higher in 2025 than in 2013. It is a defensible crash-composition measure, but it does not measure pedestrian-level risk and may rise when other kinds of crash reports fall."
+        }
+    ]
+}
+(OUT / "options.json").write_text(json.dumps(options, indent=2) + "\n")
+
+print(annual.to_string(index=False))
